newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-June 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- APPLE DAILY -- The debate between Chief Secretary Anson Chan and Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa has heated up. Chan hinted in an interview with a foreign magazine that she would quit if repeatedly asked to defend policies which went against her conscience.

-- TIN TIN DAILY --The Hong Kong government has sent out 15,000 invitations to local and international guests to three farewell ceremonies. But some, such as pro-Beijing politician Tsang Yok-shing, have already rejected the invitation.
-- MING PAO -- Beijing has sent "sensitive" students and intellectuals out of the capital "on holiday" to ensure stability during the anniversary of the Tiananmen crackdown.
-- EXPRESS NEWS --Sources said China has set out to reform its salary system, aiming to fill in the income gap which has been responsible for the dissatisfaction of many state workers.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Beijing is trying to enlarge its satellite transmission power to ensure the whole world sees the Hong Kong handover ceremony and celebrations in China and the territory.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- China Resources is rated the best quality red-chip company in Hong Kong by local investment business, followed by Cosco Pacific and China Overseas.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- China's guidelines for red-chip companies in Hong Kong are expected to be mild, so mainland capital continued to flow in to invest in red-chip shares.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- Recent Communist Party meetings in Tibet decided to strengthen control over religious affairs and crack down on splittist activities by followers of Tibetan spiritual leader Dalai Lama.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Hong Kong government plans to release 70 hectares of land for low-density residential development in the next 25 months, which will be four times the amount of land supplied for that sector in the past three years.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The stock exchange and the Securities and Futures Commission have introduced more joint interim measures to ensure retail investors were not squeezed out of new issues by international institutions.
